Ovdal-az-Ân (I19)

Region (English scoring-table division): Serpentspine.

In one sentence: Retake the “Hold of One” from the goblins, revive the Dwarven Pantheon, and turn the Tree of Stone into a sealed sanctuary defended by runes and magic.

Story: high｜Mission-tree length: medium-long (40 direct missions)｜Mission-tree update: local files support EU4 v1.37.5.0; exact rework date unresolved｜Distinctiveness: very high｜Waiting burden: high (formation entry, hold construction, and isolation requirements)｜Early pressure: high｜Expansion capacity: medium-high

Not a Dwarven country selectable in 1444

The “Ovdal-az-Ân” in the scoring table is the hold and restorable country of the Granite Dwarves in the Tree of Stone, not a Dwarven state already ruling the hold in 1444. Province 4284 is held at game start by the Chaingrasper Clan H74; I19 has only a core and country definition. You must first use a Dwarven adventurer to take the hold, then meet the administrative-technology, territorial, and adventurer-reform requirements and enact the restoration decision before changing to I19 and receiving its missions. The country-history file describes the post-formation state and cannot prove that I19 already existed in 1444.【Local history script】【Local script】

Its old history and the new country must remain separate. The English offline Wiki describes the ancient hold as a centre of Dwarven Pantheon worship, the Hall of Dagrin, and Argrâstun Cathedral; amid the wars and religious disputes of the Tree of Stone, Queen Odna II sealed the gates in 2203 BA and maintained the runic illusion with the relic Vûrodrmonir. The hold was not permanently safe: the Chaingraspers found the entrance in 1435, and captured it after a four-year siege in 1439, killing or enslaving its inhabitants. The current mission text likewise presents the 1439 goblin invasion and the destruction of its archives and temples as the restoration campaign’s past. Wiki detail supplements the setting; the playable entrance remains defined by the local decision.【Wiki source】【Local narrative text】

From ruins to sanctuary

This is not merely a story of Dwarves repairing a hold. The first stage requires reclaiming the population, clearing ruins, organising stone archives, and guarding the surrounding caverns. The memory of the old inhabitants and the labour of outside adventurers gradually shape a new Granite Dwarf community. The country then rebuilds pilgrimage centres, religious education, and hold fortifications, increasingly treating itself as the orthodox guardian of the Pantheon.【Local script】【Local narrative text】

The middle game combines faith with isolation. Missions require control of the Tree of Stone, expanded religious influence, reduced external relations, and the restoration of the hold and its church privileges; “closing the gates” is a mission gate, not merely flavour. As Argrâstun Cathedral and the sacred-relic line advance, runic defence and powerful magic become part of rule, border fortresses, and the endgame. The final missions also require a series of Vûrodrmonir spells and extensive construction in multiple holds. This is a long internal and magical engineering campaign, not a campaign that ends after taking one mountain hold.【Local script】

The most important warning is that this revival is not gentle. The first mission enables a purge directed at goblins, and later narrative openly describes outsiders as unworthy of entering the sanctuary. The country also contains positive elements: freeing Dwarves enslaved by the Command and restoring education and public construction. But its protection has strong ethnic and religious boundaries. Opposition to Dwarven enslavement must not be translated into universal opposition to slavery, and a goblin purge is not ordinary warfare.【Local script】【Local narrative text】

How to advance

The real opening challenge comes before I19 exists: choose a Dwarven adventurer able to reach the Tree of Stone, seize province 4284 from the goblins, meet the restoration requirements, and prepare for pressure from the great power to the east. After formation, restore the hold and roads, handle goblin population and defences, then expand toward key holds and rebuild the Pantheon centre. The mid- and late-game rhythm becomes construction, improvements, fortifications, and spell preparation; territorial expansion serves the isolated sanctuary and religious centre.【Local script】

Two player discussions are experience reports rather than rules: a 2025 AAR treats high fort defence and narrow terrain as the appeal of holding against superior numbers, while a 2026 discussion stresses that the formation entrance is difficult and that later missions may require control of specified mountain areas. Numbers and routes change by version; neither post proves its casualty ratios or opening plan.【Community views】

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 66/100｜Autocracy 77/100｜Magic↔Artifice 95/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 92/100)｜Pluralism 8/100.

The v2.1 value profile is evil (28/100) with a mixed trajectory.

The current Wiki supplies historical context but does not prove every mission effect. Exact paths, revisions, and scoring grounds are listed in the original Chinese research evidence and the additional English translation receipt.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and scripted effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as idea groups are filled, and the ambition applies after all seven have been unlocked. Only national ideas themselves are listed: racial, government and mission rewards are excluded. A successor’s new set does not automatically stack with its predecessor’s ideas. Descriptions may recall history or portray future ideals, and do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Native English originals are reused rather than back-translating expanded Chinese localisation. Displayed effect values are inherited from the Chinese research data; any unresolved display units remain qualified, not silently corrected.

Ovdal-az-Ân (I19) — Granite Ideas

Traditions: Granite Traditions

Effects: Discipline: +5%; Administrative advisor cost: -25%.

Idea 1: School of Dagrin

Ovdal-az-Ân was known in ancient Aul-Dwarov as the hold where faith and piety were cultivated, where every year thousands were educated in the ways of Gods. The most famed of these halls of education was the Hul-az-Dagrin, the Hall of Dagrin. Here the greatest minds were sent to learn theology, writing, and the best ways to exalt their gods of choice. Standards were strict, each body, mind, and soul carefully and exactingly measured. Flaws would not be tolerated and if they could not be hammered out upon the anvil of penance, those who bore them would be cast aside.

Effects: Missionary strength: +2%; Missionaries: +1.

Idea 2: Vûrodrmonir

Vûrodrmonir is an ancient artefact, said to be a fragment of Joztralanna herself, the Goddess of the Moon and origin of magic, leftover from the creation of Dwarvenkind. Crafted by Urisazirn in an age long before Aul-Dwarov, Vûrodrmonir allows the wielder to cast powerful magics far beyond the ability of normal mages, so long as they are capable of magic themselves. Itself a sceptre, roughly three feet long, composed of an unknown metallic material that baffled any and all metallurgists who studied it, Vûrodrmonir was the possession of the High Priest of Halanna, their symbol of power, office, and reverence.

Effects: All power costs: -2.5%.

Idea 3: The Hold of Halanna

Where others faltered in their reverence of the Old Ways, the Granite Dwarves did not. When Ovdal Kanzad cast out the faithful, Ovdal-az-Ân welcomed them with open arms. As others began to wane in their devotion and faith, they did not abandon the Gods who had seen them through trial after trial, especially Halanna, mother of all dwarves. In so doing, they were rewarded with life, even as the impious around them burned. They hid the entry to their hold when the Tree of Stone was cast down for its heresy and so remained safe for millennia more. In the granite halls of Ovdal-az-Ân they dwelled, unmoving and eternal.

Effects: True-faith tolerance: +2; Religious power modifier: +10%.

Idea 4: The Edict of Odna II

In 2203 BA, the legendary Odna II, both Queen of Ovdal-az-Ân and High Priestess of Halanna, ordered the sealing of Ovdal-az-Ân. This measure was not made lightly, but the heresy and dangers within the Tree of Stone were deemed extreme enough, to require such a drastic measure. A month-long period of solemn reflection was taken, during which time the hold's Runeworkers sealed the gate with specially runecarved granite blocks and Queen Odna used Vûrodrmonir to weave a complex spell over the gates. It was decreed, that the gates would only open again after 5,000 years had passed and the heretical world was once again safe for true believers. Thus did the Granite dwarves seal themselves off from the world, becoming as much a part of mother Halanna as the mountains themselves.

Effects: Fort defence: +15%.

Idea 5: Hold Hogs

Hold Hogs are a type of Serpentspine creature, a distinctive breed of swine that was a staple meat of ancient Aul-Dwarov, and something Ovdal-az-Ân was famed for before the Fall. After their declaration of independence from the Jade Empire, many farmers in the hold sought to alleviate manpower and supply shortages by breeding larger and stockier hogs, more fit for hauling and pulling wagons. When an outbreak of Rotheflu decimated the hold's population of Rothe, it only further cemented Ovdal-az-Ân's reputation as a hold of swine with the rest of the Tree of Stone.

Effects: Global supply limit modifier: +25%.

Idea 6: Argrâstun Cathedral

In the heart of Ovdal-az-Ân n sits a cavern of immense size, and at its heart an elegantly sculpted dagger of stone hangs from the ceiling. This is Argrâstun Cathedral, the centre of the cult of Halanna during the height of Aul-Dwarov. The stalactite, which Argrâstun Cathedral is made from, has been hollowed out into a massive temple complex dedicated to Halanna and is the seat of power from which the monarch ruled. Surrounded by dozens of other hanging temples to other gods, built from lesser stalagmites or stalactites that radiate out from it, the great cavern of Ovdal-az-Ân was a breathtaking site, with no part as wonderous or well adorned as Argrâstun.

Effects: Building cost: -10%; Clergy loyalty equilibrium: +5%.

Idea 7: Fall of Ovdal-az-Ân

In 1435 AA, the unthinkable occurred. The isolation that Ovdal-az-Ân had so long enjoyed was broken, as a horde of goblins broke through the long-unmanned gate, the illusion of Odna pierced by mere chance. Within hours, entire sections of the upper level were swarmed by goblins, who seemed more interested in taking dwarves as slaves than plundering. Thousands were captured before a proper defence could be mounted and even then, the mobilisation was slow. As the siege continued, more goblins were drawn to the hold and within a few short years, the hold of Ovdal-az-Ân had fallen. Only in the shadows did a few hardy souls remain, fighting an ever more desperate war for their survival.

Effects: War exhaustion: -0.03.

Ambition: Granite Ambition

Effects: Available administrative policies: +1.
